title: US Data Center Hiring Index
subtitle: Monthly aggregates of live US data center job postings by state, role, employer
description:
Monthly aggregate snapshot of live US data center job postings, with median advertised pay from employer-stated ranges.

Each edition is frozen at one recorded UTC cutoff and never revised. Methodology and the current edition: https://datacenterjobhub.com/data-center-hiring-index

## Files

Each edition is a folder, YYYY-MM/.

`data-center-hiring-snapshot-YYYY-MM.csv` - one row per aggregate. Summary metrics (live jobs, employers, states, city-state pairs, listings stating pay, listings published in the previous 7 and 30 days), the top 12 states, the top 12 employers, and every role family, each with its share of all live jobs.

`data-center-hiring-snapshot-YYYY-MM-pay.csv` - median advertised lower and upper bounds per role family and pay period.

`data-center-hiring-snapshot-YYYY-MM-employers.csv` - from October 2026, live jobs for every employer with a live job.

`data-center-hiring-snapshot-YYYY-MM-panel.csv` - from October 2026, the same-employer, same-method comparison with the previous edition: the only change between editions the dataset reports.

`data-center-hiring-snapshot-YYYY-MM-pay-transparency.csv` - stated-pay share by state against whether state law requires a pay range in the advertisement, with a within-employer control. It carries its own, later cutoff.

## Method

Population is the listings live and approved on Data Center JobHub at the cutoff, all in a US state; closed, expired and duplicate listings are excluded and nothing older than 90 days by the source's own posting date is carried. Job titles are grouped into broad role families by the site's title-matching rules; a job belongs to exactly one family.

Pay uses only employer-stated USD ranges carrying both bounds. Aggregator and feed estimates are excluded. Annual and hourly listings are reported separately and never converted between. A role x period row is published only at 8 or more ranges. The pay figures are medians of advertised bounds, not of earnings.

Change between editions is reported only for a panel of employers named in both editions whose boards were read the same way at both cutoffs, with their ads judged again by the title rules as they stood at the earlier cutoff.

## Limits

This is a census of the monitored listings, not of the US labour market. The monitored employer set grows over time, so totals move with coverage as well as with hiring; the difference between two editions' totals is not a trend. Monitoring began on 21 August 2026, so earlier posting-date cohorts are incomplete.

## Licence

CC BY 4.0. Attribute to Data Center JobHub and link to https://datacenterjobhub.com/data-center-hiring-index

The licence covers these aggregates. It does not extend to the underlying job listings, which belong to the employers who published them.
